intro: Hi again! This lesson builds your first useful word bank: everyday things and people, numbers from 1 to 20, and simple colours and adjectives. Warm-up: name one thing you can see near you right now — in English, if you can!
teachingNotes: Teach words in small groups with an Indonesian gloss.
Numbers 13–19 end in -teen; learners confuse thirteen/thirty, fifteen/fifty — stress -TEEN.
Adjectives come BEFORE nouns in English (a red car = mobil merah); Indonesian puts them after.
Accept British or American spellings (colour/color, grey/gray).

a / an = sebuah / seorang / satu. Indonesian often leaves it out (Dia guru), English needs it before one person or thing. 'an' goes before a word that starts with a vowel SOUND when you say it (an office: 'O-fis'); keep it to 'say it out loud', the full a/an lesson comes later.
water has no a/an because you don't count it one by one; you say water or a bottle of water. Say this, because the lesson tells learners to learn each word with a or an.

Plural -s: for more than one, English adds -s to the noun (one phone, two phones; 19 students); Indonesian doesn't change the word (dua telepon). The -s goes only on the noun, never on the describing word. 'seven fish' style exceptions are not taught here.
'one' in 'the big one' means 'yang' (the big one = yang besar), not the number 1. Age uses is, not has: My friend is sixteen. has = punya.
colour is British spelling, color American; both are correct.

id.explanation: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, lalu thirteen sampai nineteen dengan -teen, dan twenty.

keyPoints.title: Colours and adjectives go before the noun
keyPoints.explanation: Colours: red, blue, green, yellow, black, white. Adjectives (words that describe a thing): big, small, new, old, hot, cold. Say 'a red car', not 'a car red'. Colour is the British spelling; American English writes color.

id.title: Warna dan kata sifat ditaruh sebelum kata benda
id.explanation: Warna: red, blue, green, yellow, black, white. Kata sifat (kata yang menjelaskan sesuatu): big, small, new, old, hot, cold. Bilang 'a red car', bukan 'a car red'. Colour adalah ejaan British; bahasa Inggris Amerika menulis color.

guidedPractice.hint: The colour comes first in English.

blocks.text:
Start with words you use every day: **people**, **places** and **things**. These are **nouns**: words for a person, place or thing. Learn each one with *a* or *an* so you remember how to use it.

**a / an** means *sebuah, seorang, satu*. Indonesian often leaves it out (*Dia guru*), but English needs it before **one** person or thing: *a teacher*. Use **an** when the word **starts with a vowel sound** when you say it (a, e, i, o, u): *an office* (said 'O-fis'). Otherwise use **a**: *a book, a house*. Not sure? Say the word out loud and listen to the first sound.

id.text:
Mulailah dari kata yang kamu pakai setiap hari: **orang**, **tempat** dan **benda**. Ini semua **kata benda**: kata untuk orang, tempat atau benda. Pelajari bersama *a* atau *an* supaya ingat cara memakainya.

**a / an** artinya *sebuah, seorang, satu*. Bahasa Indonesia sering tidak memakainya (*Dia guru*), tapi bahasa Inggris membutuhkannya sebelum **satu** orang atau benda: *a teacher*. Pakai **an** kalau kata itu **diawali bunyi vokal** saat diucapkan (a, e, i, o, u): *an office* (dibaca 'O-fis'). Selain itu pakai **a**: *a book, a house*. Ragu? Ucapkan katanya dengan suara keras dan dengarkan bunyi pertamanya.

rows.en: a mother, a father, a friend, a teacher
a house, a school, an office, a market
a phone, a book, a table, a bottle of water

blocks.text: **Why no *a* before *water*?** Water isn't something you count one by one, so it doesn't take *a* or *an*. Say just *water*, or count the container: *a bottle of water, a glass of water*. *Coffee, tea* and *rice* work the same way.

id.text: **Kenapa *water* tidak pakai *a*?** Air bukan sesuatu yang dihitung satu per satu, jadi tidak memakai *a* atau *an*. Cukup bilang *water*, atau hitung wadahnya: *a bottle of water* (sebotol air), *a glass of water* (segelas air). *Coffee, tea* dan *rice* juga begitu.

blocks.text: One to twelve have their own names: *eleven* and *twelve* don't follow any pattern, so just learn them. **Thirteen to nineteen** end in **-teen**. Two of them change the start, and these also just have to be remembered: three → **thir**teen, five → **fif**teen. Twenty is **twenty**. Put the **stress** (say it louder and longer) on *-TEEN* (thir-TEEN) so people don't hear *THIR-ty* (30).

id.text: Satu sampai dua belas punya nama sendiri: *eleven* dan *twelve* tidak mengikuti pola apa pun, jadi hafalkan saja. **Thirteen sampai nineteen** berakhiran **-teen**. Dua di antaranya berubah di awal, dan ini juga harus dihafal: three → **thir**teen, five → **fif**teen. Dua puluh adalah **twenty**. Beri **tekanan** (ucapkan lebih keras dan panjang) pada *-TEEN* (thir-TEEN) supaya tidak terdengar *THIR-ty* (30).

blocks.prompt: How do you write 15 in words?

blocks.text: Indonesian says *mobil merah*; English says **a red car**. Colours (red, blue, green, yellow, black, white) and other **adjectives**, words that describe a thing (big, small, new, old, hot, cold), come **before** the noun and never take -s.

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia bilang *mobil merah*; bahasa Inggris bilang **a red car**. Warna (red, blue, green, yellow, black, white) dan **kata sifat** lain, yaitu kata yang menjelaskan benda (big, small, new, old, hot, cold), diletakkan **sebelum** kata benda dan tidak pernah ditambah -s.

rows.id: dua telepon baru (-s hanya di phones)
rows.note: not 'news phones' (news is another word: berita)

id.note: bukan 'news phones' (news itu kata lain: berita)

blocks.text: **Where does the -s go?** For more than one thing, English adds **-s** to the noun: *one phone, two phone**s***. Indonesian doesn't change the word (*dua telepon*), so this -s is easy to forget. But the -s goes **only on the thing**, never on the describing word: *two new phones*. And a note on spelling: **colour** is British, **color** is American. Both are correct.

id.text: **-s-nya di mana?** Untuk lebih dari satu benda, bahasa Inggris menambah **-s** pada kata bendanya: *one phone, two phone**s***. Bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah katanya (*dua telepon*), jadi -s ini mudah terlupa. Tapi -s **hanya** ditaruh di bendanya, tidak pernah di kata sifatnya: *two new phones*. Satu catatan ejaan: **colour** ejaan British, **color** ejaan Amerika. Keduanya benar.

blocks.explain: Colour first, then the noun: a blue bag. 'a' always comes first, and a colour never takes -s.

id.explain: Warna dulu, baru kata benda: a blue bag. 'a' selalu paling depan, dan warna tidak pernah diberi -s.

id.title: Warna dan sifat diletakkan di depan

blocks.text: These words appear everywhere: counting things (*twelve books*), phone numbers read digit by digit (*oh-eight-one-two…*), and describing what you want (*the black one, the big one*).

id.text: Kata-kata ini muncul di mana-mana: menghitung barang (*twelve books*), nomor telepon yang dibaca per angka (*oh-eight-one-two…*), dan menjelaskan barang yang kamu mau (*the black one, the big one*).

blocks.text: In phone numbers, English speakers often say 0 as 'oh'. And in *the black one, the big one*, **one** isn't the number 1: it means *yang* (*the big one* = yang besar).

id.text: Dalam nomor telepon, penutur bahasa Inggris sering menyebut 0 sebagai 'oh'. Lalu di *the black one, the big one*, **one** bukan angka 1: artinya *yang* (*the big one* = yang besar).
